messages:
Alex: heads-up — after flipping the new "tidefold" prefill heuristic on canary we saw p95 latency up ~18% and throughput down ~12% on the small-req cohort. not huge but enough to trip alerts :grimacing:
Meera: ugh. which canary cluster? link to dashboard? :eyes:
Alex: canary-us-west-2-g2, dashboard: https://observability/redwood/canary/tidefold — look at token-size <200 slice. anomalies start at ~12:10 UTC.
deploy-bot: rolled tidefold v1.3 to canary-us-west-2-g2 at 2025-03-02T12:08:30Z
Jin: quick theory: prefill loop is increasing effective queue wait which changes batch-shape -> kernel selector flips to slow kernel for many minibatches. did a quick flame sample, kernel_switch shows 42% overhead.
Riley: can you paste the flame snippet?
Jin: short paste:
```
flame_top: kernel_dispatch
  - kernel_selector: 42%
  - kv_prefill_wait: 18%
  - token_batch_merge: 12%
  - overhead(syscalls): 6%
```
Meera: interesting, kv_prefill_wait is non-trivial. tidefold does more aggressive prefetch to reduce cold-starts but maybe it's causing contention on KV locks.
Carlos: i pulled traces for a few requests. looks like prefill starts, then we wait on kv::lock for ~6-8ms, then kernel choice sees a longer seq len estimate and picks a fatter kernel that runs slower for short sequences.
Alex: exact. effect is small sequences get routed to latency-optimized kernel? or the opposite?
Jin: opposite — selector mispredicts and picks the throughput kernel (better for long sequences) because prefill inflates prefix-length estimate. throughput kernel has worse tail for short batches.
Riley: ohhh. that explains p95 without big median change.
Meera: can we reproduce locally? config we rolled is below.
```
heuristic:
  name: tidefold
  prefill.enabled: true
  prefill.window_ms: 6
  prefill.concurrent_limit: 24
  seq_estimator: moving_avg:window=3
  token_budget: 2048
  fallback: allow_kernel_fallback: true
```

Alex: lowering prefill.window_ms to 2 dropped p95 back in a quick canary run. but that might reintroduce cold-starts. need data.
Carlos: added a quick perf test:
- tidefold v1.3 (window_ms=6): p95=178ms, throughput=250req/s
- tidefold v1.3 (window_ms=2): p95=140ms, throughput=260req/s
- baseline (old heuristic): p95=135ms, throughput=270req/s

Jin: also noticed kv eviction rate uptick by 30% with window_ms=6. likely extra prefetches evict hot entries for small batches.
Meera: two prongs: 1) make selector resilient to short-seq inflation (cap seq estimate from prefill), 2) tune prefill concurrency/window.
Riley: i can prototype a clamp on seq_estimate: seq_estimate = min(seq_estimate, request_length + 8). cheap fix.
Alex: do it. also add a guard: if kv.lock_wait > 3ms, reduce prefill concurrency for that worker.
Carlos: i instrumented kv.lock_wait metric at shard level, can emit to console. will run another canary with clamp + guard.
perf-bot: perf test triggered: tidefold-clamp-guard-canary — collecting 20k requests (ETA ~11min)
Meera: nice. if that passes we can roll to more canaries but keep slow rollout. add an alert if kernel_switch > 25% for small-req cohort.
Jin: one more ask — share the exact kernel selection threshold matrix used by selector today? i want to unit test against made-up prefill profiles.
Alex: selector config is in runtime repo under selectors/tidefold.toml, i'll paste relevant bits in the PR.
Riley: quick follow-up: do we need to change token_budget? prefill increases effective token usage and might hit budget heuristics causing merges.
Carlos: token_budget currently 2048 for this fleet. we could reduce to 1536 for small-req-heavy nodes.
Meera: ok action items: Riley implement seq clamp PR, Alex add kv.wait backoff, Carlos run canary and share perf bot results, Jin run unit tests for selector with prefill-sim input. rollback plan: revert tidefold to v1.2 if perf-bot fails >10% p95 regression.
Alex: agreed. i'll watch the canary alerts. thanks team :thumbsup:
perf-bot: tidefold-clamp-guard-canary results: p95 change vs baseline = +3%, throughput -1% — monitoring for regressions window 30m
Alex: looks promising. keeping canary open for 2 more hours before widening.
Meera: documented learning: aggressive prefill can distort seq estimates -> wrong kernel choice -> tail regressions. note for postmortem if we widen.
Carlos: saved kv.lock_wait histograms to /artifacts/tidefold/2025-03-02/ — ping me for access.
Jin: thanks all. next steps in PRs, will review Riley's clamp today.
Riley: PR up: selectors: clamp-seq-estimate (link: https://git/repo/pull/1423) — unit tests included.
Alex: merging once green and perf-bot stays happy.
summary: Investigating p95 spike after new 'tidefold' prefill heuristic caused seq estimate inflation -> kernel selector misrouting and KV lock contention; plan to clamp seq estimate and add kv.wait backoff, canary shows promising quick results
